description: 2008 is the Year of the Earth Rat in the Chinese zodiac, from February 7, 2008 to January 25, 2009. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 2008 is the Year of the Earth Rat, a Yang year. It began at Lunar New Year on February 7, 2008 and ended on January 25, 2009, so people born in 2008 before Feb 7 belong to the Fire Pig year.

sections.heading: 2008 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Earth Rat year on February 7, 2008, and the year ran to January 25, 2009. So a birth date of Feb 7, 2008 or later counts as Earth Rat, and so do early 2009 birthdays through Jan 25; births in 2008 before Feb 7 still belong to the Fire Pig. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1948 are Earth Rat years too. That Thursday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Earth Rat is like
paragraphs: Think of an Earth Rat as a strategist with a long view. With Earth channelling the Rat's Water, the sign's restless cleverness is said to settle into careful, patient planning. Those born now are often reliable, sensible and fiercely protective of home security. Generosity and small, deliberate changes are the classic antidotes to the worry and tight grip this combination can develop.

In classical thought, Earth belongs to the centre and to the late-summer pause between seasons, the point where things ripen and settle. As a year stem, it tends to slow an animal down in a useful way, adding prudence, loyalty and a strong sense of responsibility. People born under an Earth stem are often described as dependable, sensible and protective of the people they love. They value security and tend to build carefully. The caution traditionally attached to Earth is caution itself: overthinking, clinging to the familiar and carrying other people's problems as though they were their own.

sections.heading: 2008 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the year's digits reduce to 1, the number of beginnings, initiative and independence, so numerologists describe a 1 year as one that rewards starting things. The digits of 2008 add up to 10, which reduces to 1. The Rat holds the first place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Water. Set beside the year's Earth stem, earth controls Water, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Fire Pig and the year after is the Earth Ox.

Chinese almanacs name 2008 Wu-Zi, pairing the Earth stem Wu with the branch Zi. Both are Yang, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 2008?
faq.answer: 2008 is the Year of the Earth Rat. It started on February 7, 2008 and ended on January 25, 2009.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 2008?
faq.answer: Check the date against Feb 7. Born before February 7, 2008, you are a Fire Pig; born on or after it, you are a Earth Rat.

faq.question: What element is 2008 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Earth, a Yang year. The Rat's own fixed element is Water; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 2008?
faq.answer: Wu-Zi. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Earth Rat year?
faq.answer: 2068, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1948.
